mainEntity.name: Limbo
mainEntity.description:
Austin Wright grew up in Cardiff, where he attended night classes at the Cardiff School of Art before studying Languages at New College, Oxford. Entering a career in teaching, he came to Yorkshire in 1937, and in 1946 settled with his wife Sue in Upper Poppleton, where he stayed for the rest of his life. He created his sculptures in the barn and garden of their 18th-century home, and by 1954 had given up teaching to concentrate on his art. Initially influenced by Moore and Hepworth, he became known for his small lead figure groups. Between 1961 and 1964 he was Gregory Fellow in Sculpture at the University of Leeds.

Limbo gathers 26 lead pieces created from drawings and observations made in sketchbooks on family seaside holidays in Anglesey and Cornwall in the 1950s. One drawing from the early 1950s is marked ‘Limbo’ and ‘Praa’ (a beach on the south coast of Cornwall), and some of these figure sketches relate directly to those in this sculpture, which for many years was displayed on the corner of the patio in the family garden at Upper Poppleton.
